claims.text: On October 29, 2026 the builder @khushjammu wrote that he had enjoyed Link balance and, because it runs on Tempo, had traced its funds flow onchain; his write-up is titled "Inspecting my Link Balance onchain."
Link says a user's balance is held as USDC and settled on Tempo, Stripe's payments-focused chain.
A merchant is paid through a one-time card, not a chain transaction.
Tempo's stated reasons are 24/7 settlement, sub-cent fees paid in stablecoins and reserved payment blockspace.
The user is "responsible for all purchases your agent makes."
Link balance launch Oct 26, 2026 (stat: 'Instinct first, eligible US users'); Tempo page does not call Instinct the first partner, only the named rollout app.

The funding path, as summarized by one secondary source, runs: debit-card top-up, conversion by Stripe's onramp into a dollar stablecoin on Tempo, a Privy-powered wallet behind the Link account, an agent-wallet limit, then a Stripe-issued virtual card for the purchase.
The Link FAQ confirms the part users see: funds are held in USDC, and receipts show USDC even for card-funded balances.
Instinct is a text-message assistant; a Brazilian report quotes its founder as saying users spend over US$1,300 a month through the agent.
US$150 per setup link; Amex, Discover, Capital One unsupported; 18+ and SSN verification.
Spend request ceiling 50,000 cents (US$500); the request moves through ten statuses from created to succeeded or failed.
Tempo frames the problem the same way, with concert presale tickets and price-drop shoes as the time-sensitive buys that stall behind a human approval.

The open-source Link CLI hands agents one of three credential types: a virtual card, a Link Pay Token for supported Stripe surfaces, or a Shared Payment Token for merchants using the Machine Payments Protocol.
The user approves each request through a push notification with a 30-minute window, and the tool is currently limited to US and Canadian Link accounts.
Stripe sells the needed USDC, funds a prepaid card account at Lead Bank, and payment runs over Visa to the merchant's processor, so merchants need no wallet or stablecoin support.
Stripe's Issuing documentation confirms the generic capability: virtual cards, spending controls and real-time authorizations delivered by webhook.
Tempo has no native gas token. The explorer page notes the currency symbol is USD and that account funds are held as TIP-20 balances.

The fee spec quotes fees in attodollars per gas, caps the base fee at 12 billion attodollars per gas and floors it at 600 million. On those parameters a roughly 50,000-gas TIP-20 transfer costs about 600 microdollars ($0.0006) at the cap and about 30 microdollars ($0.00003) at the floor.

Fee payment follows a precedence: transaction field, account preference, TIP-20 transfer token, DEX swap input token, then a pathUSD fallback. If the user's token differs from the validator's preferred token, the Fee AMM converts at a fixed 0.9970 rate per hop, a 0.3% spread that stays in the pool.
The fee spec states a 500M total block gas limit with 30M for general use, so about 94% of blockspace is reserved for payments and 6% left for general computation.

A transaction qualifies only if every call matches an allow-listed payment call shape and its access list and authorization lists are empty; payment transactions can use remaining block capacity; no separate base-fee rule is stated.
TIP-20 adds fixed 32-byte memo fields (transferWithMemo) and a shared policy layer; token issuers get pause, burnBlocked and burnAt roles and transfer-policy hooks, with decimals() fixed at 6.
Consensus is Simplex BFT via Commonware with "deterministic sub-second finality".
Link says pending merchant charges can sit up to seven days before an authorization expires.
Overall spend "varies by behavior and agent," resets daily and cannot be raised. [^3,5]
Approval for each purchase requires biometric sign-off in the standard flow, though the FAQ gives both a 30-minute and a 10-minute expiry.
Link says withdrawals to a bank take 3–5 business days and crypto withdrawals usually minutes, with no fee for crypto withdrawals; failed transfers that never reached the chain return to the balance.
With a per-purchase cap, orders under the cap skip approval, and a $0 limit restores approval on every purchase; the cap is per purchase and the funded balance is the only cumulative ceiling.

In the custodial model, Bridge, a Stripe company, holds the USDC and manages the private keys; in the self-custodial model, Link and Privy provide an onchain wallet whose private key can be exported; launch materials do not say which version Instinct users receive.
Stripe agreed to buy Privy in June 2025, a wallet infrastructure provider with 75M accounts, and it already owned the stablecoin company Bridge.
Tempo's mainnet went live on March 18, 2026, built by Stripe and Paradigm after roughly three and a half months of testing.
On April 14, 2026, The Block reported that Visa, Stripe and Zodia Custody by Standard Chartered signed on as early validators, moving beyond an "initial small circle of operators."
The network itself is described as moving toward more validator partners and eventually permissionless validation. [^13]
Tempo raised $500 million at about a $5 billion valuation in October 2025 in a round led by Thrive Capital and Greenoaks, and neither Stripe nor Paradigm invested in that round.

The OCC issued its final implementing rule on October 21, 2026, and both the rule and the Act take effect January 18, 2027; the separate Treasury-coordinated rulemaking will cover BSA, AML and sanctions.

Circle shows reserve categories as of October 26, 2026, with most held in the Circle Reserve Fund managed by BlackRock; Deloitte & Touche is auditor and a September 2026 examination report is the latest linked.
Developer daily limit (CLI README) $500.
Whether MPP, co-developed by Stripe and Tempo and currently running only on Tempo, begins to carry agent purchases directly instead of through a card.

One search result describes Instinct as having a US$2.5 billion valuation, while a secondary summary reports a US$1 billion raise at a US$10 billion valuation; neither was verified against a primary filing. [^2]
Timeline: Tempo mainnet + MPP (2026-03), Visa/Stripe/Zodia validators (2026-04), Stripe agrees to buy Privy (2025-06), Link balance launches Oct 26 with Instinct as first partner.
The seed tweet is dated October 29, 2026 (20:23 UTC) and links to the article; Link balance has drawn hype on FinTech Twitter and the UX is smooth.
